`mad_qc()` flags selected tails of numeric metrics. A flag is evidence of
statistical atypicality within the supplied reference distribution, not a
diagnosis of cell quality.

| Direction | Flagged values |
| --- | --- |
| `lower` | Below the lower limit |
| `upper` | Above the upper limit |
| `both` | Outside either limit |

Limits are estimated as the median plus or minus `nmads` scaled MADs after any
transformation. By default, `nmads = 3` and the MAD constant is 1.4826.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(veryMAD)
```

## Missing values and threshold status

Missing metric values receive `NA` flags. The combined flag is `TRUE` if any
metric is flagged; if none is flagged, it is `NA` when any metric flag is
unresolved.
Because the combined flag uses an OR rule, its flagged fraction can rise as
more metrics are included. Review per-metric counts alongside it.

The example uses percentage points for `pct_mito`: 8 denotes 8%.

```{r}
qc_metadata <- data.frame(
  sample = paste0("sample_", 1:7),
  library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 2.8e6, 0.5e6, NA_real_),
  detected_genes = c(12000, 12500, 13100, 12800, 13400, 1600, 12200),
  pct_mito = c(4, 5, 6, 5, 7, 8, 30)
)

qc_result <- mad_qc(
  qc_metadata,
  metrics = c(
    library_size = "lower",
    detected_genes = "lower",
    pct_mito = "upper"
  ),
  output = "report",
  verbose = FALSE
)

qc_result$flags[, c("id", "library_size", "detected_genes",
                    "pct_mito", "mad_qc_outlier")]
```

The threshold report gives `status`, limits on raw and transformed scales,
and counts of reference, flagged, and unresolved observations.

```{r}
transformed_result <- mad_qc(
  qc_metadata,
  metrics = c(library_size = "lower", pct_mito = "upper"),
  transform = c(library_size = "log1p"),
  output = "report",
  verbose = FALSE
)

transformed_result$thresholds[, c(
  "metric", "direction", "transform", "lower_raw", "upper_raw",
  "status", "n_used", "n_flagged", "n_unresolved"
)]
```

`min_n` defaults to 5 non-missing reference observations per metric and group.
Groups below this size have `insufficient_n` status; groups with no observed
values have `all_missing` status.

## Zero MAD

A zero MAD provides no estimate of non-zero spread. Choose how to handle it:

| `zero_mad` | Behavior in `mad_qc()` |
| --- | --- |
| `"na"` (default) | Leave flags unresolved |
| `"zero"` | Set the selected limit at the median and flag values beyond it |
| `"error"` | Stop |

## RNA and ATAC metrics

The following directions are common starting points, not universal rules.
Metric definitions and their relationship to biology depend on the assay,
protocol, and sample.

| Modality | Example metric | Example direction | Example transformation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RNA | `nCount_RNA`, `nFeature_RNA` | `lower` | `log1p` |
| RNA | `percent.mt` | `upper` | `none` |
| ATAC | `nCount_peaks` | `lower` | `log1p` |
| ATAC | `TSS.enrichment` | `lower` | `none` |
| ATAC | `nucleosome_signal` | `upper` | `none` |

For example, in droplet RNA-seq, mitochondrial percentage can reflect cell
damage, but it may also vary with cell type or biological state. ATAC metrics
also depend on how peaks, TSS enrichment, and nucleosome signal were defined.
Inspect distributions by sample and known cell groups before filtering.

```{r}
rna_metadata <- data.frame(
  sample = rep(c("sample_A", "sample_B"), each = 6),
  nCount_RNA = c(820, 910, 970, 1050, 1120, 100, 125, 150, 175, 190, 210, 230),
  nFeature_RNA = c(430, 480, 520, 570, 610, 55, 80, 95, 100, 115, 125, 140),
  percent.mt = c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 35, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9)
)

rna_report <- mad_qc(
  rna_metadata,
  metrics = c(
    nCount_RNA = "lower",
    nFeature_RNA = "lower",
    percent.mt = "upper"
  ),
  transform = c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p"),
  output = "report",
  verbose = FALSE
)

rna_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "transform", "status")]
```

```{r}
atac_metadata <- data.frame(
  nCount_peaks = c(1200, 1800, 3200, 6000, 9000, 20000, 2500, 4100),
  TSS.enrichment = c(0.8, 1.3, 3.0, 5.4, 8.0, 15.0, 4.1, 6.2),
  nucleosome_signal = c(3.5, 2.4, 1.8, 1.4, 1.1, 0.9, 1.6, 1.3)
)

atac_report <- mad_qc(
  atac_metadata,
  metrics = c(
    nCount_peaks = "lower",
    TSS.enrichment = "lower",
    nucleosome_signal = "upper"
  ),
  transform = c(nCount_peaks = "log1p"),
  output = "report",
  verbose = FALSE
)

atac_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "transform", "status")]
```

## Batch and reference thresholds

`batch` estimates limits separately within each label. `subset` selects the
reference observations used in each group; flags are still returned for all
observations. Define a reference set independently of the QC metrics when
possible, since metric-based selection can bias the limits.

::: {.callout-warning}
MAD limits describe the reference distribution, not an external quality
standard. If most reference cells are poor, their values still define the
baseline. Batch-specific limits can also miss a uniform shift across a batch.
Inspect distributions by batch and cell type; add absolute criteria only when
supported by the assay or protocol. [OSCA basic discusses these adaptive QC
assumptions](https://bioconductor.org/books/3.23/OSCA.basic/quality-control.html#quality-control-motivation).
:::

The 416B [OSCA workflow](https://bioconductor.org/books/3.23/OSCA.workflows/lun-416b-cell-line-smart-seq2.html#quality-control)
illustrates QC metrics across plates with batch information. `veryMAD` uses
MAD-based thresholds on supplied metrics; it does not reproduce
`scuttle::quickPerCellQC()`.

```{r}
rna_annotated <- mad_qc(
  rna_metadata,
  metrics = c(
    nCount_RNA = "lower",
    nFeature_RNA = "lower",
    percent.mt = "upper"
  ),
  transform = c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p"),
  batch = rna_metadata$sample,
  verbose = FALSE
)

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plot_mad_qc(rna_annotated,
              c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"),
              batch = rna_metadata$sample)
}
```

## Seurat metadata

`mad_qc()` accepts a Seurat object and adds flags to cell metadata; it does not
calculate QC metrics. For mitochondrial percentage, define a species- and
assay-appropriate feature set and use [`Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet()`](https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/percentagefeatureset)
with the intended assay. Check feature identifiers and denominator: the
function divides selected-feature counts by all counts in the chosen assay and
reports 0–100%.

This synthetic example checks that annotation preserves cell order and accepts
a reference set defined before QC.

```{r}
if (requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)) {
  counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
    seq_len(40) %% 6,
    nrow = 5,
    sparse = TRUE,
    dimnames = list(paste0("gene-", 1:5), paste0("cell-", 1:8))
  )
  seurat_object <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)
  seurat_object[["percent.mt"]] <- c(4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 30)
  seurat_object$sample <- rep(c("sample_A", "sample_B"), each = 4)
  seurat_object$reference_cells <- c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE,
                                     TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)
  cell_ids <- colnames(seurat_object)

  seurat_annotated <- mad_qc(
    seurat_object,
    metrics = c(
      nCount_RNA = "lower",
      nFeature_RNA = "lower",
      percent.mt = "upper"
    ),
    transform = c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p"),
    batch = seurat_object$sample,
    subset = seurat_object$reference_cells,
    min_n = 3,
    verbose = FALSE
  )

  stopifnot(identical(rownames(seurat_annotated[[]]), cell_ids))
  head(seurat_annotated[[]][, c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA",
                                "percent.mt", "mad_qc_outlier")])
}
```
